name: Jonas Dhaenens
forbes_bio: Jonas Dhaenens is founder of team.blue, a software platform designed for owners of small to medium businesses and marketing agencies.
He started the precursor to the copmany, Combell, at age 16 in Belgium.
Team.blue now operates in 22 countries and serves a customer base of 3.3 million, according to its website.

name: Hans Langer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Hans Langer is the world's first 3-D printing billionaire.
Langer founded EOS, one of the earliest and most successful 3-D printing companies, more than 30 years ago.
Daughter Marie Langer took over as CEO of the largest operating business, EOS GmbH, which makes 3D printers for polymers and metals, in October 2019.
While others focused on consumers and 3-D printing, Langer always believed that the technology's true value was in industrial applications.
Venture capital firms have plowed funds into American 3D printing startups, but the Langer family has turned down investments and sales offers.
forbes_facts: Langer's first customer was BMW, which bet on EOS before it even had a product available.
He has turned down multiple, multi-billion-dollar acquisition offers, insistent that the business stay in the family so that he can run it as he wishes.

name: David Beckham
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2015)
forbes_bio: Soccer great Sir David Beckham made a fortune on and off the field during his two-decade playing career, and has continued to rake in big money since retiring in 2013 at age 38.

Beckham has inked lucrative endorsement deals with the likes of Adidas, Hugo Boss and Tudor Watches. In 2019, he sold 55% of his brand business to Authentic Brands Group for $250 million in cash and stock.

His biggest bet has been on Major League Soccer. He shocked the sporting world when he agreed to leave Real Madrid for the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2007, lured in part by an option to purchase a future MLS expansion team for a mere $25 million.
His current 26% stake in the team he helped create, Inter Miami, is now his largest single asset. Forbes most recently valued the team at $1.35 billion.
Beckham grew up in London's East End, the son of the father who fixed and serviced gas ovens, and a mother who was a hairdresser. He married Spice Girl and model Victoria Adams in 1999.

name: Amanda Westphal Radcliffe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Amanda Westphal Radcliffe owns 21% of publicly traded tax solutions provider Vertex Inc.
The Pennsylvania-based company was founded in 1978 by Westphal Radcliffe's parents, Ray and Antoinette Westphal.
Westphal Radcliffe and her two siblings, Jeffrey Westphal and Stefanie Westphal Thompson, purchased the company from their parents in 2000.
Together, they took the company public in 2020. Westphal Thompson is also a billionaire.
Westphal Radcliffe sits on Vertex's board of directors.

name: Kevin Plank
sec_insider_companies: Under Armour, Inc. (UA) - President and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Under Armour founder Kevin Plank built the popular sportswear brand as the underdog competitor to Nike.
Noticing his football teammates' sweat-soaked shirts, Plank came up with a lightweight, sweat-wicking shirt using fabrics from women's undergarments.
In the mid-1990s he sold his first shirts from his grandmother's basement, exaggerating to early customers to make the company sound bigger.
Plank, who stepped down as Under Armour's CEO in 2019 but returned to the role in 2024, took the company public in 2005.
forbes_facts: Plank got kicked out of his high school after an alcohol-fueled brawl with Georgetown U football players; he later walked onto the U. of Maryland's football team.
Plank served on President Trump's manufacturing council but resigned in 2017 after the president lightly criticized neo-Nazi protestors in Charlottesville, Virginia.
